Question: A book that is to be recorded onto compact discs takes \(412\) minutes to read aloud. Each disc can hold up to \(56\) minutes of reading. Assume that the smallest possible number of discs is used and that each disc contains the same length of reading. How many minutes of reading will each disc contain?
Solution:
First determine how many whole discs are needed. Since
\[
412=7\cdot56+20,
\]
seven discs leave \(20\) minutes unrecorded. Eight discs can hold \(8\cdot56=448\) minutes, so eight is the smallest possible number.

Sharing the reading equally among those discs gives \(412\div8=51.5\) minutes per disc. This is below the \(56\)-minute capacity, so the equal allocation is possible. Each disc contains \(\boxed{51.5}\) minutes, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
